title: Should the trailing-stop staircase scale with each stock's own ATR%, instead of a fixed percentage for everyone?

tables.name: ATR-scaled staircase configs vs fixed baseline (3 tested)

notes: Multiplier = candidate's own ATR% (predictor.py's compute_volatility_pct(), same definition/window the live volatility exclusion filter already uses) divided by the cross-sectional median ATR% among that day's scored candidates -- self-normalizing to the day's relative volatility spread rather than an arbitrary fixed reference. Capped to avoid a single extreme-ATR ticker producing a degenerate staircase. Only TRAIL_STEPS is scaled; STOP_LOSS_PCT stays fixed at the live -3% (repeatedly reconfirmed well-calibrated elsewhere in this project).

conclusion.summary: 0/3 ATR-scaled staircase configs beat the fixed baseline on win_rate AND avg_pct, both TRAIN and VAL.
